There is an indication on the map of equidistances, and as I said, those are vertical distances between two neighbouring isohypses. And on the set of five maps, it is ten metres. On maps 1:50000 and 100000, this equidistance is 20 metres. And on a map of 1:200000, which is still a topographic map, the equidistance is 100 metres. Why. Because it covers a larger area, and simply it is readable and usable.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. So let me try to see if I understood what you've told us, sir. In producing the maps that we have before us in the binders, you relied on the locations, that is the A and the B points were provided to you by the Defence, and all the other information you were able as a professional topographer to determine from the face of the paper map itself.

utterances.speaker: ABID IZMIRLIC
utterances.text: Absolutely so. If you were to give me a map of The Hague and if you were to tell me to select two particular points, with the help of the map I would be able to tell you whether visibility is possible or not. I don't have to go to the spot to be able to tell you that. In every army in the world there is a service known geotopographic security of the armed forces and which any normal commander has to use before any action. And also in the broader senses, in order to decide whether he will use tanks along a particular axis. A tank cannot go across gorges. It cannot jump over. If he gives them the wrong direction, they would all fall in. So he has to study the map carefully to see whether the terrain is such as to use armoured mechanised units, where he will build engineers' fortifications, et cetera. So every branch of the army will decide accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, I think it will be best to stop because it is almost a quarter to two. I have something to ask the registrar regarding the programme for tomorrow. So, Witness, your testimony will continue tomorrow so you will be spending the evening in The Hague. So I will ask you to come back for the hearing tomorrow morning at 9.00. In the meantime you will not meet with the Defence attorneys, because having taken the solemn declaration, you are now a witness of justice and you are not allowed to contact anyone before tomorrow. I will ask the you canner to escort you out of the courtroom and the witness and victims unit will take care of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. Is it tomorrow or Monday as somebody said to me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A priori you will be testifying tomorrow. In principle, you will not be here until Monday unless the Defence expects to keep you until Monday through the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, regarding the question of documents, the Judges have the impression that there's a slight confusion regarding P662. There are two memos of the CLSS which were given number C-10. So this morning we asked that we address an additional request to the CLSS with two questions, and when we receive the answers to those questions there will be a third memo which will remain marked C-10, regarding DH270, and that was the document given the code C-10. Is that all clear, Mr. Registrar? Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I agree with the two references that you made. It is quite clear now. C-8 and C-10. It's only P491/E and DH270/E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Having said that, I ask everyone to come back tomorrow for the hearing at 9.00 to hear the witness who will come earlier than planned and then we will continue with this witness if we have time. So we will all meet again tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: be reconvened on Friday, the 4th day of March, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 25
